label: Aksum
notes: Capital city of the Aksumite Kingdom; modern Axum in northern Ethiopia

label: Adulis
notes: Principal Red Sea port of the Aksumite Kingdom; near modern Massawa Eritrea

label: Beta Giyorgis
notes: Hill site on western edge of Aksum; major multi-period occupation sequence

label: Gobedra
notes: Rockshelter site near Aksum; Pre-Aksumite and earlier occupation

label: Matara
notes: Major Aksumite site in Eritrea; excavated 1959–1965 by Anfray

label: Yeha
notes: Pre-Aksumite site ca. 35 km northeast of Aksum; Temple of the Moon

label: Hawulti-Melazo
notes: Site near Aksum with early Aksumite material; stele and votive objects

label: Dungur
notes: Locality in western Aksum; site of the Dungur palace complex

label: Mezber
notes: Site in the Tigray highlands; Pre-Aksumite and early Aksumite occupation; excavated by Fattovich

label: Ona Nagast
notes: Site near Beta Giyorgis; monumental platform structure excavated by Sernicola

label: Nefas Mawcha
notes: Location of the fallen Great Stele (Stele 1) in the Northern Stelae Field

label: Enda Mikael
notes: Locality in Aksum with sub-surface architectural remains excavated 1993–1997

label: Northern Stelae Field
notes: Monumental cemetery zone north of Aksum town centre; UNESCO World Heritage Site

label: Tigray region
notes: Northern Ethiopian highland region; core territory of the Aksumite Kingdom

label: Eritrea
notes: Modern state; corresponds broadly to northern periphery of Aksumite territory

label: Mai Shum
notes: Locality in Aksum; site of a large rock-cut reservoir attributed to the Aksumite period

label: King Ezana
notes: Aksumite king r. c. 325–360 CE; issued trilingual inscription; converted to Christianity

label: King Kaleb
notes: Aksumite king r. c. 514–540 CE; led campaign into South Arabia; canonised as saint

label: King Endubis
notes: Earliest Aksumite king known to have minted coins; c. late 3rd century CE

label: David W. Phillipson
notes: British archaeologist; directed 1993–1997 British Institute in Eastern Africa excavations at Aksum

label: Rodolfo Fattovich
notes: Italian archaeologist; directed excavations at Mezber and Ona Nagast

label: Luisa Sernicola
notes: Italian archaeologist; excavations at Beta Giyorgis and Ona Nagast reported in Sernicola et al. 2019

label: Kathryn A. Bard
notes: American archaeologist; co-director of Aksum-area survey and excavations

label: Pre-Aksumite period
notes: c. 800–100 BCE; characterised by South Arabian cultural influences, temple architecture at Yeha

label: Proto-Aksumite period
notes: c. 100 BCE–100 CE; transitional phase; reduction of South Arabian influence, emergence of distinctly Aksumite material culture

label: Early Aksumite period
notes: c. 100–350 CE; growth of urban centre; first coinage (Endubis); monumental stelae erected

label: Classic Aksumite period
notes: c. 350–550 CE; apogee of Aksumite power; coinage of Ezana; Christianisation; maximum urban extent

label: Late Aksumite period
notes: c. 550–700 CE; Aksumite power contracting; decline of Red Sea trade; possible Kaleb-era monumental works

label: Aksumite period
notes: c. 1st–7th century CE; general label for the entire span of the kingdom; used when finer periodisation is not attested

label: Post-Aksumite period
notes: c. 700–1000 CE; period following the fragmentation of centralised Aksumite authority; Lalibela-era antecedents

label: Great Stele (Stele 1)
notes: Tallest Aksumite obelisk at c. 33 m; now fallen and broken; Northern Stelae Field

label: Stele 2
notes: Second-tallest Aksumite obelisk at c. 24 m; removed to Rome 1937; returned to Aksum 2008

label: Stele 3
notes: Third-tallest Aksumite obelisk still standing at Aksum; c. 21 m high

label: Ezana Inscription
notes: Trilingual royal inscription (Ge'ez / Sabaean / Greek) recording Ezana's military campaigns

label: Endubis gold coin
notes: Gold coin of King Endubis; earliest known Aksumite coinage type; c. late 3rd century CE

label: Ezana coin (pre-Christian)
notes: Bronze coin of King Ezana bearing crescent-and-disc symbol before Christianisation

label: Aksumite fine ware
notes: Handmade buff-ware ceramics characteristic of Aksumite domestic assemblages at Beta Giyorgis

label: Beta Giyorgis lithics
notes: Obsidian and chert knapped stone assemblage from Pre-Aksumite levels at Beta Giyorgis

label: Iron slag assemblage
notes: Iron-working debris recovered from Aksumite activity surfaces at Ona Nagast

label: Glass bead assemblage
notes: Import trade goods; glass beads of Mediterranean or South Asian origin found at Matara and Adulis

label: Aksumite bronze lamp
notes: Cast bronze lamp of Aksumite type; recovered from urban context at Aksum

label: Mausoleum (Tomb of Brick Arches)
notes: Subterranean royal tomb complex beneath the Northern Stelae Field; multiple chambers

label: Dungur palace
notes: Large multi-roomed stone structure at Dungur; interpreted as an elite residence or palace, c. 4th–6th century CE

label: Church of St. Mary of Zion
notes: Cathedral attributed to 4th-century construction under Ezana; rebuilt multiple times; legendary Ark repository

label: Beta Giyorgis terrace complex
notes: Sequence of artificial terraces on the slopes of Beta Giyorgis hill; Pre-Aksumite to Aksumite occupation

label: Ona Nagast platform structure
notes: Monumental stone-built platform at Ona Nagast; possibly a Proto-Aksumite ceremonial structure

label: Tomb of Kaleb and Gebre Meskel
notes: Rock-cut tomb complex traditionally attributed to King Kaleb and his son; in northern Aksum

notes: Layer 4 Beta Giyorgis; Proto-Aksumite context; calibrated using IntCal20

label: OxA-7847 charcoal Beta Giyorgis
notes: Layer 2 Beta Giyorgis; Early Aksumite context; calibrated using IntCal20

label: Beta-95230 organic Dungur
notes: Floor context Dungur palace; Classic/Late Aksumite; calibrated using IntCal20

label: OxA-1023 charcoal Gobedra
notes: Gobedra rockshelter; Pre-Aksumite Iron Age context; calibrated using IntCal20
